catalogue.note: Read from Figma at real size (375×800, nothing scaled): auto-layout frames are flex with Figma’s direction, gap, padding and alignment, everything else sits at its Figma offset, and all 76 boxes land on Figma’s to 0.05px. Square-cornered: the frame’s own 16px corners are left off and the diff leaves the four corners out (308 pixels). Kept as Figma renders it, flaws included. The orange “Withdraw ₦6,500” button (24,403 327×56) lies over the grey card (24,275 327×149): it covers the card’s last 21px and the bottom 2px of the fee line “Total will include ₦500 fee” (ink y 397.6 to 405.1), whose letters are cut at y 403. The frame holds two keyboards in the same place, both starting at y 475, 46px above the top of the frame that holds them (0,521): the iOS instance “NumericKeyboard” (46:48365, 375×279) lies wholly under the Android set (46:48867: toolbar 42, keyboard 241, bottom nav 42, 375×325), which is opaque. What shows, and what is built, is the Android one; the iOS one is not drawn. So an Android keyboard and Android bottom nav sit under an iOS status bar. The title is at y 110 here against 118 on the other two old screens. “₦30,000” (22px, 33-high box) and “Current Balance” (14px, 21-high box) are top-aligned, so their baselines are 9px apart. Keyboard digits are live Roboto 400 25px; the keys with symbols, the toolbar icons and the nav icons are Figma’s SVG export, shadows included. The naira sign is not in Satoshi (the files on this Mac hold no U+20A6) and Figma draws it from a fallback face: each one is Figma’s own outline of the glyph, inline, 0.572em wide. The iOS status bar is Figma’s SVG export: the time (SF Pro Text Semibold 17) as Figma’s outline, signal, wifi and battery as its vectors. Baselines: Figma rounds a line’s baseline to a whole pixel where Chrome rounds ascent and descent apart; the 23px title, the 19px nav title and the 28px amount sit 1px lower than Chrome puts them, and the button label lands on a half pixel that Figma draws on the row above (−0.5px). The offsets are Figma’s baseline (its render bounds plus the glyph height from the font file) minus Chrome’s, not fitted to the picture. What is left in the diff is glyph and curve edges: Figma’s rasteriser against Chrome’s. Flat fills match exactly.
